title: Audio library
summary: Recordings of papers and books, verbatim or summarized, to listen to anywhere.
description: Papers read aloud, and summaries of several. Each work has one reading, verbatim, started from the work at any of its sections and made as it's listened to, on whichever device plays it; summaries are recordings of their own, kept with where they came from. What's made syncs to every device for listening offline, on a phone with the screen off.

requirements.text: The audio library holds the library's readings and its summaries, newest first; each opens in a player. An item's reading is also started from the item.

history.text: The audio library holds recordings of the library's papers and books, newest first; each opens in a player.
history.reason: A reading belongs to the work: a section and the whole paper were recordings of their own, listed apart and made twice.

requirements.text: Each item has one reading, verbatim, made as it's listened to. The author starts it from the item: where it was left, at its beginning, or at any section of its contents, down to the smallest, and it plays on into the sections after. Its sections are its chapters.

history.text: The author can record an item verbatim, whole or one of its sections from its contents, down to the smallest; the sections within a recording are its chapters.
history.reason: A reading belongs to the work: a section and the whole paper were recordings of their own, listed apart and made twice.

requirements.text: A verbatim recording reads the text as written. Formulas are said the way a mathematician reads them aloud, and figure captions are read; the authors, their institutions and contact details, the bibliography, page numbers, running heads and footnote marks are not.

requirements.text: The author can record a summary of one or more items, read by one narrator, at a length from `audio.summary-lengths`: what the works say, never who wrote them; the summary's parts are its chapters.

requirements.text: Recordings are spoken by `audio.speech-model` through OpenRouter, in a voice the author picks, and their text is prepared by `audio.script-model`; both can be changed in Settings, and their use is logged in the ledger.

A recording is made as it's listened to: on whichever device plays it, `audio.lead` ahead of where the author is, its text prepared and spoken a passage at a time. Paused, it stops once that much is made; skipping to a part not yet made waits while that part is made. What's made is kept, so nothing is made twice, and making carries on where it was when the app starts again.

history.text: A recording is made on any device, in the background while the app runs, and shows how far it has come; if the app stops, it carries on from where it was without speaking again what was already spoken.
history.reason: Making a whole recording before any of it could play kept the author waiting minutes, and paid for parts never listened to.

requirements.text: Recordings are kept as Opus in WebM, mono at `audio.bitrate`, a passage at a time as they're made, and what's made syncs to every device for listening offline.

requirements.text: The player plays, pauses, seeks, skips between chapters, and plays at a speed from `audio.speeds`.
Where the author stopped listening is kept and syncs, so a recording carries on from there on any device.
On a phone, a recording keeps playing with the screen off and the app in the background, with lock-screen, notification and headphone controls, which skip between chapters too.
On a computer, the keyboard's media keys control the player.
The player's address holds the recording and the moment playing, `#t=<seconds>`.

The author can have the rest of a recording made at once, for listening offline: on the device that asked, in the background while the app runs, showing how far it has come, and carrying on after the app stops.
Nothing already made is made again: a passage spoken in a voice is used again wherever it recurs, and an item's recordings from before it had one reading become part of its reading.

history.text: What one recording has made is used again by another, not made twice: recording a section and then the whole paper, the section's text isn't prepared again, and a passage already spoken in the same voice isn't spoken again.
history.reason: A reading belongs to the work: a section and the whole paper were recordings of their own, listed apart and made twice.

requirements.text: A reading is in the voice it was started in. Read in another voice, it starts afresh: what was spoken in the old voice goes, and its prepared text stays.

A summary is kept with its script and where it came from: the works and which of their texts it read, the script model and what it was told, its length, the speech model and voice, and when and on which device it was made. Its recording shows them. A reading keeps, for each part of its text, the model that prepared it.

A reading follows its item's text: when what it was prepared from changes (a fresher version of the item, or a better way of reading it into chapters), it's prepared again, and what was made of the text that didn't change is kept.
The player's chapters show how much of each is made, and the author can have a chapter made now, ahead of listening to it.
